findings.title: Do not debit before rejecting a locked destination
findings.explanation: The new placement of the destination-lock validation makes a transfer mutate the sender before a documented failure is thrown. For a funded source and a destination whose account ID starts with `locked-`, `transfer` throws `destination locked` after decrementing the source, while never crediting the destination. This is a current-head, PR-introduced violation of failed-transfer atomicity; the two breadth candidates are the same root cause.
findings.failurePath: `transfer(accounts, fundedSourceId, lockedDestinationId, cents)` passes the existence and funds checks, executes `from.balanceCents -= cents`, then throws at the locked-destination check. The caller observes failure but the in-memory ledger retains the debit. Restore validation before either balance mutation (or make the mutations atomic) and add a behavior test asserting both balances are unchanged after this error.
